title: Ryobi USB Power Cutter 2Ah Kit $69 (Was $89) + Delivery ($0 C&C/ in-Store/ OnePass/ $99 Power Tools Order) @ Bunnings
body:
Deal: Ryobi USB Power Cutter 2Ah Kit $69 (Was $89) + Delivery ($0 C&C/ in-Store/ OnePass/ $99 Power Tools Order) @ Bunnings

[nocure] Suitable for cutting plastic, carpet, rubber, leather, paper, cardboard
[anthman] These are ~$35-40 on AliExpress after GST and before any cashback. No removable battery. USB c chargeable.
[GreenLego] Did a search and came up straight away:
https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005012347458350.html
even cheaper on Amazon:
https://www.amazon.com.au/Electric-Scissors-Rechargeable-Car…
[twocsies] I found one for $38 on AliExpress but the reviews were not pretty.
It arrived broken with the box crushed
M***z, 20 May 2026
0 *
Useless device that struggles to cut more than 20mm
****e, 28 May
[Lucille Bluth] I mean 2cm is pretty thick for a device like this for the purpose it was designed for.
[Vodafail] Either we’re incredibly lazy or we’ve engineered ourselves into inefficiency, we’ve outsourced the simple act of cutting to a battery because we can’t be trusted with scissors anymore.
[jjjaar] Or maybe people with limited dexterity, strength and/or chronic pain in their hands are able to maintain independence and still cut things themselves without having to ask someone to cut something for them?
If you don’t understand a product that seems like a gimmick, it’s not for you… yet.
[MaXcon] That's like saying why drive a car when you can walk 🤦🏻‍♂️
[ifreddo] Or why sex a girl when you can sex a meow meow.
[Sped1] I dont know man. I get that many amazon boxes ive gotta get down to strips to get into yellow bin. This is awfully tempting.
[pdtmathieson] I got one of these or similar from Amazon Japan ages ago for about $5
https://www.amazon.com.au/This-DC-191C-Hasegawa-cutlery-card…
Chews up cardboard, easy to cut boxes down to a few pieces laying flat. Good if the kids want to make something about of a box too, it's pretty safe to wield.
[Lucille Bluth] Have fun breaking apart that box your next fridge comes in with just scissors instead of using a device like this that makes the job much more easier and quicker cutting the cardboard into 20+ of smaller pieces to fit into recycling.
[Averell] These days cardboards are used instead of styrofoam. I have 5-10cm thick cardboard pieces that I don't know how to cut.
Can I cut those using this tool?
[Averell] @Vinnie Vegas: Nah. I'm not the why-this-not-scissors guy.
[revheadgl] Cut capacity on this is rated at 6.4mm max. Which is about right in my experience. They will cut through a heavy duty moving carton but they are starting struggle a bit.
For thick stuff, I find a reciprocating saw is the go, Best to cut over a bin as they make a bit of a mess though.
[w3n] I love how they’ve marketed it with a guy using it to cut wrapping paper and wearing safety glasses.. but no hand protection whatsoever.
[faricity] They have also dropped the price on extra batteries. $29.99 to $19.99 for a single and $49.99 to $29.99 for the double pack.
The extra batteries i believe dont directly fit into the tools. They are just power banks that will charge other devices.
[revheadgl] I have one as a spare and they do fit, They just have the added feature of being able to reverse charge via usb.
[PCHammond] Ive got one of these. Initially found it fun and useful.
Quickly came to realise that a box cutter (stanley knife) was much faster and less cumbersome.
[tomee] Thanks for that. I was going to purchase for this and have always used a sharp box cutter
[GordonD] Everyone realises don't they that even if you put paper or cardboard in the recycling bin the sorting process means it ends up in landfill if its not above a certain size.
If you have a box or something like that that you need to open it up and put it in the bin like that, in one piece, not cut it up into a lot of little pieces that won't get recycled.
[Averell] I've always been curious about the sorting process. What would they do with boxes having plastic stickers, tapes,…
